severityGuide.note: WCAG has no severity scale; it only says pass or fail. A criterion fails if it has any finding, whatever the severity. Severity sets the order to fix things in and how much each finding lowers the score.

levels.critical: Blocks the task: someone can't finish it at all (e.g. font scaling turned off app-wide).
levels.high: A major barrier that's hard to work around (e.g. a button with no name, a field with no label).
levels.medium: A real problem with a workaround, or one that affects fewer people (e.g. a button that doesn't announce its role).
levels.low: Minor friction (e.g. heading-styled text not marked as a heading).

sources.how: axe's own impact rating: critical → Critical, serious → High, moderate → Medium, minor → Low.
A fixed severity for each Lighthouse audit, set by the toolkit.
The severity the tester chose. An issue written without one is Low. A check marked failed with no description at all uses that check's default severity.

keyTakeaway: 2 high-severity issues create barriers on this page. Fix first: Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds.

principleSummaries.P: Most serious: Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds; Background and foreground colors do not have a sufficient contrast ratio..
principleSummaries.R: Most serious: Heading levels should only increase by one; Document should not have more than one banner landmark.

findings.title: Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds
findings.description: Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds

findings.title: Heading levels should only increase by one
findings.description: Ensure the order of headings is semantically correct

findings.title: Document should not have more than one banner landmark
findings.description: Ensure the document has at most one banner landmark

findings.title: Document should have one main landmark
findings.description: Ensure the document has a main landmark

findings.title: Landmarks should have a unique role or role/label/title (i.e. accessible name) combination
All page content should be contained by landmarks
findings.description: Ensure all page content is contained by landmarks

findings.title: Background and foreground colors do not have a sufficient contrast ratio.
findings.description: Low-contrast text is difficult or impossible for many users to read. [Learn how to provide sufficient color contrast](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.12/color-contrast).

findings.title: Heading elements are not in a sequentially-descending order
findings.description: Properly ordered headings that do not skip levels convey the semantic structure of the page, making it easier to navigate and understand when using assistive technologies. [Learn more about heading order](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.12/heading-order).

findings.title: Document does not have a main landmark.
findings.description: One main landmark helps screen reader users navigate a web page. [Learn more about landmarks](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.12/landmark-one-main).

conformance.text: WCAG conformance is all or nothing: to meet Level AA, every applicable Level A and AA criterion must pass. There is no partial pass. Criteria that don't apply (N/A or web only) count as met. So far 0 of 55 applicable criteria pass; 3 fail and 52 aren't verified yet.
conformance.scoreNote: The accessibility score is not a pass mark. It measures how many issues remain, weighted by severity, so it can be 0 when a few shared fixes would clear most failures, or in the 90s while one failure still blocks conformance.

footer: Automated checks only (axe-core, Lighthouse) on https://www.bluetread.com/. Automated scanners cover roughly 30–40% of WCAG success criteria; keyboard, screen reader, zoom, and content review weren't part of this quick scan. A full audit is needed to confirm conformance.
